ev.q: Among 5,221 hospitals, 3,787 (73%) reported having a committee that monitors and reviews sepsis care.
Among these hospitals, 3,787 (73%) reported having a sepsis committee.
Fifty-five percent of all hospitals provided dedicated time (including assigned protected time or job description requirements) for leaders of these committees
Prevalence of these committees varied by hospital size, ranging from 53% among hospitals with 0–25 beds to 95% among hospitals with >500 beds.
Having no standardized process was more common in hospitals with 0–25 beds (15%) than in hospitals with >500 beds (1%).
Descriptive analysis, stratified by hospital size (number of beds), was completed on a data set generated on June 1, 2023
These committees were least common in hospitals with 0–25 beds (53%), and progressively more prevalent as hospital size increased

public_health_question.v: What is the prevalence and what are the characteristics of sepsis programs in U.S. acute care hospitals in 2022, overall and by hospital size?

ev.q: The 2022 National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN) annual survey evaluated the prevalence and characteristics of sepsis programs in acute care hospitals.
Sepsis Program Activities in Acute Care Hospitals — National Healthcare Safety Network, United States, 2022
This survey of the majority of U.S. hospitals describes the current state of sepsis programs and identifies potential areas of improvement.
Enrolled hospitals were required to complete the 2022 NHSN Patient Safety Component Annual Hospital Survey by March 1, 2023.

equity.level_reason: The unit is the hospital; results are stratified only by hospital size, which is not a social-position dimension. No SPD of patients is defined or analyzed.

notes: Purely descriptive survey of hospitals; the six hospital-size groups are compared side by side with no tests or CIs. Design inferred as cross-sectional from the single-year survey; free-text 'Other' responses were excluded for low response (an exclusion rule, not a procedure).
view_issues: Tables label the largest size group '>501' beds while the text and Summary say '>500'. The ** note repeats the New York regulations URL.
